title: perf: performance canary - adaptive auto-detection and rollout guards
author: Ava Patel
release_notes: Implements adaptive auto-detection for performance canaries and tighter rollout guards to reduce noisy rollouts and prevent regressed model variants from reaching production traffic.
description:
Motivation: We continue to see intermittent latency regressions pass through canaries due to static thresholds and noisy short-lived spikes. This PR implements adaptive thresholding + hysteresis and tighter rollout guards to reduce false positives and prevent regressions from reaching production.

What changed: 1) Adaptive detector that computes per-model rolling baseline (p50/p95/p99) and derives thresholds from both absolute and relative deltas. 2) Hysteresis window and minimum sample periods to avoid reacting to transient spikes. 3) Traffic gating: canary rollout now requires sustained pass for both latency and throughput metrics and cross-checks with a lightweight distributional regression test before increasing traffic. 4) Operator-visible metrics and dashboard tiles added for transparency (detector confidence, baseline drift, guard decisions).

Rollout plan: staged rollout to perf-canary fleet over 48 hours with initial conservative thresholds (alpha=0.7). Monitoring dashboard and alerting configured; emergency toggle added to console for immediate rollback.

Testing: unit tests for detector math, e2e perf canary integration on perf-canary cluster, and offline validation against historical traces (backfill for last 30 days). Benchmarks show reduced false-positive gating by ~42% on historical traces.

Related work: Linear ENG-4821 (canary auto-detection), ENG-4920 (rollout guard UX), Jira SUP-2134 (customer incident referencing canary leak).

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration tests - [x] Benchmarked against historical traces - [x] Documentation updates - [x] Console toggle for emergency rollback

Notes: Description and implementation avoid changing public API surface; configuration flags default to previous behavior unless enabled via feature flag.
